sections.content: You know participles such as *hablado* and *escrito* from A2 Unit 1. A few verbs have two: a regular one in *-ado* or *-ido* and a short one inherited from Latin. After *haber* both are correct: *He imprimido el informe* and *He impreso el informe* mean the same, and with *freír* the short form is in fact the more common one (*He frito el pescado*). As an adjective, including after *estar*, the short form is the usual one: *el informe está impreso*, *patatas fritas*, *la tienda está provista de agua*. It is worth learning only the common pairs below; other verbs have just one participle.

sections.title: The common pairs
rows: he imprimido / he impreso el informe; un libro impreso
he freído / he frito el pescado; patatas fritas
he proveído / he provisto la comida; una tienda provista de agua
elegir: elegido (electo is only an adjective)
han elegido a la alcaldesa; la alcaldesa electa

items.english: We have already printed the tickets.

items.spanish: El presidente electo visitó la escuela.

sections.content: A safe rule: after *estar* and before or after a noun, use the short form (*frito*, *impreso*, *provisto*). After *haber*, either form is correct. *Electo* is not a participle at all: it only describes someone elected who has not yet taken office, and after *haber* the verb is always *elegido*.
